edges.effect_quant: Dose-response meta-analyses backed by prospective cohorts suggest a clinically meaningful but not extreme effect, especially in higher-risk or more exposed groups.
edges.mechanism: Dietary fat class alters lipoprotein metabolism, hepatic lipid trafficking, and membrane signaling in different directions: saturated fats tend to raise LDL particle burden, while mono- and polyunsaturated fats usually improve the substitution pattern. For LDL cholesterol, the biologic effect is driven less by total fat and more by what carbohydrate or fat source is displaced.
edges.summary: Dose-response meta-analyses backed by prospective cohorts link high saturated fat intake to higher ldl cholesterol in general adult. The average effect is usually moderate rather than dramatic, so this edge is better read as a risk modifier than a stand-alone cause or cure.
edges.caveats: Dose, timing, and baseline risk still matter. Observational edges may partly reflect broader lifestyle patterning, while small trials can overstate benefit if follow-up is short.
